summary: @kropa/baileys ships char-code-obfuscated exfiltration endpoint and obfuscated license guard
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that injects hidden network behavior into its message-send path. lib/Socket/messages-send.js line 425 assembles a destination URL via String.fromCharCode(...) that decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/ — a host unrelated to the upstream Baileys project and reconstructed from a numeric array rather than appearing as a plain string literal. The same file assembles the host again at line 436. lib/Utils/license-guard.js is heavily obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers (_0x1e6253, _0x1d5468, etc.), concealing additional logic. The combination of char-code-obfuscated destination reconstruction inside a messaging library's send path and an opaque guard module is consistent with covert exfiltration of caller-handled WhatsApp session/message data to an author-controlled endpoint, with obfuscation specifically used to hide the destination from casual review of the fork.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
